channel.title: Tire Guides — Abu Al-Ragheb Tires
channel.description: Jordan's multi-brand tire, wheel and battery specialist since 1963 (Haitham Abu Al-Ragheb Sons Co.): five branches in Amman, Faz3a 24/7 roadside service, fleet and government supply, and B2B supply in the UAE.

item.title: How to read your tire size
item.description: What every number on a tire sidewall means — width, profile, rim size, load index and speed rating — and where to find your car's correct size.

item.title: When should you replace your tires?
item.description: Replace tires at 1.6 mm tread, at five to six years old, or at the first crack or bulge — whichever comes first. How to check each one yourself.

item.title: How old are my tires? Reading the DOT code
item.description: Find the four-digit DOT date code on your tire sidewall: 2324 means week 23 of 2024. How old is too old, and why fresh stock matters in Jordan's heat.

item.title: What tire pressure should I use?
item.description: Use the pressure on your door sticker, check it cold once a month, and expect it to rise in summer heat. A practical tire pressure guide for Jordanian drivers.

item.title: Wheel balancing vs wheel alignment
item.description: Vibration at speed means balancing. Pulling to one side or a crooked steering wheel means alignment. How to tell which one your car needs.

item.title: Tire care in Jordan's summer heat
item.description: Hot asphalt, long drives to Aqaba and the Dead Sea, and full cars: seven tire checks that prevent summer blowouts in Jordan.

item.title: All-terrain vs mud-terrain tires
item.description: Wadi Rum sand, rocky wadis or Amman traffic? How all-terrain and mud-terrain tires compare on grip, noise, wear and comfort — and which one suits you.

item.title: Premium, mid-range or value tires?
item.description: Pirelli or a value brand? What you get for the extra money, when a value tire is the smart choice, and how to check any tire meets DOT/ECE standards.

item.title: Flat tire? What to do, step by step
item.description: Get safe, decide whether to change the wheel or call for help, and avoid ruining a repairable tire. Faz3a 24/7 reaches you within 45 minutes inside Amman.

item.title: Tire Rotation: Why, When and How Often
item.description: Front tires wear faster than rear ones. Rotating every 8,000–10,000 km evens out wear and gets more life from a set. How rotation works on FWD, RWD and 4x4.

item.title: Best Tires for Hot Weather in Jordan
item.description: What makes a tire good in Jordan's heat: heat-resistant compounds, the right load and speed rating, fresh DOT dates and correct pressure. How to choose.

item.title: Summer vs All-Season Tires in Amman
item.description: Summer or all-season tires for Amman? How each performs in Jordan's hot dry summers and short, sometimes icy winters — and which suits your car.
